newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares boosted by higher chemical stocks.
newsitem.headline: German shares boosted by higher chemical stocks.

text.p: Dealers were hoping for increased volumes in German share trade over the rest of the week as chemical shares gave the IBIS DAX index much-needed impetus to push the market higher on Tuesday afternoon.
The IBIS DAX index was up 10.52 points at 2,564.94 points in late electronic trade.
"The market is trading 100 percent on fundamentals at the moment as interest rate fantasy disappears -- it's all company news," said one trader.
The trader added that trading volumes were better than Monday's year-low levels.
However, the trader said volumes still left much to be desired and the market needed a sustained burst of healthy trading volumes.

"We'll probably do 5.5 or six billion marks today, but that's rubbish compared to what we had at the beginning of the year. The undertones are firm-ish but we need volumes to be higher for a few days.
"Without sustained volumes you don't have the business," said the trader.
BASF AG was the heaviest-traded stock in afternoon IBIS trade.
"It's very selective out there at the moment, but BASF is doing twice the volumes anything else is doing," said one trader
Dealers said the interest in chemical stocks was coming from foreign investors.
Hoechst went higher after a report in the German business magazine Capital said its operating profits were set to increase to 4.6 billion marks in 1996.
Other corporate news moving the market included half year figures from Linde AG, which reported an eight percent increase in pre-tax profits to 262.1 million marks.

BASF was up 65 pfennigs at 44.39 marks, while Hoechst was up 1.02 marks at 52.57 marks. Linde shares were down 8.25 marks at 922.75 as its first half profit rise was below analysts' forecasts of an 11 to 20 percent increase.
Truck and engineering group MAN AG reported a 21 percent increase in net profit to 300 million marks in 1995/96. MAN shares traded 15.30 marks higher at 368.10 marks in afternoon trade.
Shares in tyre-maker Continental AG went higher after it reported a doubling of its first-half pre-tax profits to 120 million marks.
Continental shares closed at 25.10 marks, up 20 pfennigs.
